decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: 'The notes, archiving, and importing are useful additions but not part of the essential first version.' Round 2 client: 'I agree the notes, archiving, and importing can come later.'
decisions.note: Specification-gate scope decision. Maker's presented v1 scope omits extended reference items (note markdown REF-BM-23; archive/reverse-vs-delete/archive-list REF-BM-26/27/28; import REF-BM-30). Client explicitly names these three feature areas and accepts their deferral without requesting alignment — an observable requirement expression that reveals the requirements without implementing them.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: 'saving begins from an always-visible address box'. Round 4 client: 'I liked that the address box is right there at the top ready to go' — save from a URL works.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-URL conforms to REF-BM-01.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents only 'title, description' auto-fill ('the title/description filled in on their own'); no favicon or preview image. Round 4 client lists what was seen: 'the site it came from, a clear title, a short description... and when I saved it' and approves ('exactly enough').
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting title, description, favicon AND preview image. Presentation omits favicon/preview image (preview image never appears in any round). Client approves without expressing the missing metadata → passes unexpressed; approval alone does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: 'searches titles, descriptions, and source sites without caring about capitalization'. Round 5 client: 'it didn't matter that I typed it in capitals... it searches the title, the description, and the site'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive full-text over title/description/url conforms to REF-BM-12/13 for built fields (note-search unavailable is downstream of the accepted note deferral, not a separate divergence).

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker positively scopes search: 'the first version searches titles, descriptions, and source sites' (plain substring). Round 5 client: 'This is what I wanted for finding a saved page' with no mention of #tag/boolean/phrase syntax.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reference core items REF-BM-14 (#tag syntax), REF-BM-15 (AND/OR/NOT + parentheses), REF-BM-16 (quoted-phrase exact match) are implicitly excluded by the presented simple-substring scoping. Client approves without surfacing the difference → unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: 'bookmarks can carry multiple tags and... clicking one immediately shows only bookmarks with that tag, with Show all'. Round 6 client: 'clicking Design narrowed the collection down to just the pages tagged that way'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Multiple tags per bookmark (REF-BM-09) and select-tag-to-filter (REF-BM-11) conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker uses a prepared draft that adds a new 'Reference' tag ('draft=1'); no typed tag-entry/autocomplete shown in any round. Round 12 client: 'the new Reference tag appeared alongside the others' — approves without mention of autocomplete.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-10 (offer existing tags as autocomplete on entry) is never demonstrated; tag entry always uses prepared drafts. The autocomplete behavior is absent and passes without any client expression → unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker: 'setting a bookmark aside keeps it in the full collection and also adds it to a separate read-later pile'. Round 7 client: 'the page still stayed in my main collection... the read-later count went up'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark read-later (REF-BM-17) conforms. The A/B card-action variants are functionally-equivalent UI and excluded as orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker: 'this separate view contains the page you set aside and excludes the rest'. Round 8 client: 'showed just the one page I'd set aside and left out the rest'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Separate unread/read-later view (REF-BM-18) conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker: 'this removes the page from the read-later pile but does not delete it'. Round 9 client: 'the read-later pile emptied out... still lives in my overall bookmarks'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark-as-read removes from unread list only (REF-BM-19) conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker presents duplicate handling that keeps one card and shows 'already saved... pointed me to the existing bookmark' but no edit entry point. Round 10 client: 'Ideally, from there I'd be able to jump straight into editing that existing one if I wanted to tweak it.' Round 11 maker then delivers 'Edit existing' from the duplicate notice.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-06 requires guiding the user to EDIT the existing bookmark; the round-10 presentation stops at a duplicate notice short of that. Client surfaces the gap and requests the missing reference-conforming continuation (edit the existing) → extend. Linked disposition delivered in round 11 (counted once here, as the round-11 revised presentation is recorded separately as conforming).

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker: 'Edit existing... open the existing bookmark directly, with its address, title, description, and tags available to change'. Round 11 client: 'Clicking Edit existing opened the bookmark that was already saved, with its address, title, description, and tags all right there.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Revised presentation fulfilling the round-10 extend request; converge-to-edit (REF-BM-06) and editing fields (REF-BM-04) conform. Recorded as the linked disposition, not a new opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker: 'the existing card changes, keeps the collection count at one, and displays the new tag'. Round 12 client: 'updated the existing card in place — the new title showed up and the new Reference tag appeared... still counted just one bookmark'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Edit title and assign tag in place (REF-BM-04/09) conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker presents a confirmation safeguard before deletion; Round 14 completes: 'only that bookmark disappears and the other three remain'. Round 14 client: 'Confirming the delete removed just that one bookmark and left the other three exactly as they were.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delete a bookmark (REF-BM-05) with permanent-delete confirmation conforms; the A/B deletion-safeguard variants are functionally-equivalent (both permanent delete) and excluded as orthogonal.
